findings.reason: the section names one mechanism for a rule that needs two different evidence sources, so the dispatched node must choose between a silent omission and breaking the snapshot filter's contract, and either choice is wrong for one of the section's own cases.
findings.text: §102 says `review-ready`, `promotable-stale` and `promotable` "join `LIVE_POINTER_DUTY_KINDS`'s treatment: such a duty is listed only while the run's live pointer exists and no ledger row records its promotion", but that treatment is a single `stat`: `without_departed_run_duties` drops a row only on `str(row.get("kind")) in LIVE_POINTER_DUTY_KINDS and not live_pointer_path(run_id).exists()` (`reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1053-1062`), and the banner above the set (lines 1010–1028) states the module "must not import that derivation: the hook loads this file by path so the prompt path reaches no plan, backend or ledger module" and that a missing pointer "says nothing about" any other kind — "hiding one on a `stat` would be a silent omission rather than a settlement". The ledger clause cannot be evaluated there, so a node must either extend the stat filter without it — dropping the duty for every run whose pointer vanished, including one that ended unpromoted, the omission the banner forbids — or add the ledger read the module exists to avoid; the plan states which surface owns the ledger condition and does not say.

findings.reason: without this case the gate cannot distinguish the rule the section states from the one-characteristic rule a stat-only filter gives, which is exactly the divergence that decides whether an unpromoted ended run vanishes from the view.
findings.text: §102's done-when builds only three cases: pointer gone with a promotion in the ledger, pointer present with no ledger row, and a `review-missing` duty that must survive. The rule it states ("listed only while the run's live pointer exists and no ledger row records its promotion") also withdraws the duty for a run whose pointer is gone and whose ledger records no promotion, and that case is never built — an implementation that extends the stat-only filter and ignores the ledger entirely passes all three while silently dropping the duty for a run that ended without promoting.

findings.reason: the two readings differ by whether every automatic repair round blocks the coordinator's turn, which is the same hook-blocking injury §102 exists to remove, so the kind's membership must be declared rather than inferred by the dispatched node.
findings.text: §103 introduces a duty kind that "carries no next command, because the reflex owns the round" and never says whether that row holds a stop open; the module carries a declared vocabulary for exactly this distinction — `NON_BLOCKING_DUTY_KINDS` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:178`), whose comment says the kinds in it "are listed but never hold a stop open: the work behind them is already owned by a reflex that retries, so blocking would ask the coordinator to act on a wait it cannot shorten" — and the new kind is not stated to join it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `obligation_snapshot.py`'s `LIVE_POINTER_DUTY_KINDS` is at line 1029 exactly as cited, `obligations.py` 1060–1190 holds the review-duty derivation whose docstring says a gone pointer "keeps the classifier's reading", and `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py` exists and is the reflex that resumes the reviewed worker.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §102's three cases never build "pointer gone and no ledger row records its promotion", the only case that discriminates between the two rules its deliverable states.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections' gates are pytest files under `tests/` plus a ruff delta on the staged paths; neither sends evidence to a scratchpad or a node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `repair-round` extends the existing hyphenated duty-kind vocabulary, both test filenames name the behaviour, and no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol; the section numbers appear only as plan-prose cross-references.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §102 tells the three kinds to join `LIVE_POINTER_DUTY_KINDS`, but that set is defined as a stat-only filter in a module built to read no ledger, while the rule §102 states needs a ledger row read; §103 leaves unsettled whether its new reflex-owned kind holds a stop open.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §102 lands one rule (a promoted run owes no promotion duty) with its one test; §103 lands one row kind (`repair-round`) with its one test. §103's "the ticker counts it as working" is already true of a resumed run, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the document's new `plan-section-depends-on` entry `s103: [s102]` is correct: both sections write `reckon/crew/obligations.py`, so §103 must not be admitted before §102; `s102` correctly declares no dependency and waits on no live plan.
